item.title: Austin Regular Meeting: March 26, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin City Council agenda in 3-5 bullet points: * **Housing & Development Reforms:** The Council will consider major changes to city zoning rules to allow more diverse housing types (like townhomes and small multi-unit buildings, also known as "missing middle housing") and mixed-use developments. They will also discuss reducing parking requirements, unbundling parking costs from rent, and making it easier for small businesses to operate from homes. * **Future of Transportation:** A public hearing will be held on adopting the **Austin Core Transportation Plan**, which updates the city's overall mobility strategy and comprehensive plan. * **City Boundary Changes & Disannexations:** Several public hearings are scheduled to consider removing numerous properties from Austin's city limits, primarily under the new state law (Senate Bill 1844). * **Homelessness Strategy:** Council members will vote on the adoption of the **Austin Homeless Strategies and Operations 2025-2027 Strategic Plan**, outlining the city's approach to addressing homelessness. * **Sign & Billboard Regulations:** Public hearings will address proposed changes to rules for existing off-premise signs (billboards), including relocation and height, and the authorization of new larger, electronic signs in public areas.

item.title: Austin Austin Housing Finance Corporation: March 26, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin Housing Finance Corporation agenda: * **Affordable Housing Funding**: The Austin Housing Finance Corporation Board will consider a significant financial commitment to expand affordable housing options in the city. * **$3.5 Million Loan Approval**: Board members are set to vote on authorizing a loan of up to $3.5 million for the "Sunday Village" project. * **New Affordable Units**: This funding is earmarked for National Church Residences to develop or preserve affordable housing units located near 1026 Clayton Lane.

item.title: Austin Work Session: March 24, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin City Council agenda: * **Tackling Homelessness:** Council will discuss a 2025-2027 Strategic Plan outlining new approaches and investments to address homelessness in Austin. * **Major Housing & Development Changes:** Significant amendments to land development rules will be considered to promote "missing middle" housing (like townhomes and cottage courts) and mixed-use developments combining residential and commercial uses. * **Public Hearing on Sign Regulations:** A public hearing will be held on proposed changes to city code that could allow larger, electronic, and off-premises advertising signs in public areas. * **I-35 Cap & Stitch Update:** Council members will receive a briefing on recommendations for the high-profile I-35 Cap and Stitch project.

item.title: Austin Regular Meeting: March 12, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin City Council agenda: * **Massive Wastewater Plant Expansion:** Council will consider a $600 million increase for the Walnut Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant expansion, raising the total project cost to $1.5 billion, and approve a loan of up to $1 billion to help fund it. * **Golf Course Land Use Change:** A resolution will be voted on to initiate rezoning for the 445-acre Jimmy Clay and Roy Kizer Golf Courses, potentially paving the way for future development. * **Lobbyist Transparency Rules:** Proposed changes to City Code would strengthen lobbyist regulations by revising the definition of "City Official" and requiring more detailed reporting on communications with city officials. * **Multiple Zoning and Development Hearings:** Numerous public hearings are scheduled for various neighborhood and city-wide zoning changes, including shifts to mixed-use and commercial designations, impacting several districts and specific development projects.

item.title: Austin Austin Housing Finance Corporation: March 12, 2026
item.description:
Here's a summary of the Austin Housing Finance Corporation agenda: * The **Austin Housing Finance Corporation** will meet to consider financial investments in local housing. * The main item is a proposed **$5.5 million loan** for "The Bloom at Lamar Square," a new multifamily rental development. * This project, located near 1326 and 1328 Lamar Square Drive, aims to provide additional housing options in Austin.
